key_points: Superradiance creates gaps and Regge trajectories in black-hole mass-spin space.
Self-interactions can trigger Bosenova collapse when cloud self-attraction exceeds gravitational binding.
Observed high spins can impose upper bounds on axion-like particle parameters.
Exclusion regions are naturally represented as probability/exclusion functions over boson mass.
Multiple-field exclusion probabilities can be built from single-field overlap integrals when self-interactions are weak.
68% and 95% exclusion summaries are standard outputs.
The gravitational fine-structure parameter scales as alpha ~ G M mu.
A gap in the black-hole mass-spin plane is a primary observable signature.
Stellar-mass black holes probe roughly 1e-14 to 1e-10 eV boson masses.
Linear analyses neglect nonlinear self-interaction backreaction and motivate explicit limitations statements.
Supermassive black-hole observations can provide stringent bounds on massive bosonic fields.

effect_on_contract: Need source-specific and combined exclusion-probability artifacts versus boson mass.
